explanation: The function \( \cos(x) \) is one of the fundamental trigonometric functions, representing the cosine of an angle \( x \) measured in radians. It describes the ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse in a right triangle. The cosine function is periodic, with a period of \( 2\pi \), and its values range from -1 to 1. The graph of \( \cos(x) \) is a wave-like curve that oscillates between these values, starting at 1 when \( x = 0 \). Cosine is widely used in various fields, including physics, engineering, and computer science, particularly in modeling oscillatory phenomena.
